clue.text: She's the all-round champion

definitions.text: She's the all-round champion

parts.note: all-round reads as a sporting all-rounder, but it means her curves: the winner of a beauty contest judged on her figure

explanation.surface: A tribute to a woman who excels at every sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-round' suggests versatility at games; here it is her rounded figure, the vital statistics a beauty pageant once judged.
explanation.definitionFit: The title goes to the winner of the international beauty pageant, a champion of curves.

clue.text: Her mother takes 6s!

annotationWithheld.why: Her mother takes 6s! (5): the scan confirms the text, but no reading of the cross-reference to 6 (CUPID or CORK) builds or defines MAVIS, and no source explains it

clue.text: The one to follow

definitions.text: The one to follow

parts.note: reads like advice about a leader worth following, but means the person who comes after, taking over a post

explanation.surface: Pointing out a leader whom others should follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To follow' looks like 'worth following'; it means 'coming next in line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever takes over a role after the current holder comes next in order.

clue.text: It's capital to get a post in March

definitions.text: It's capital to get a post in March

parts.words: It's capital to get a post in March
parts.note: a capital city that has its own Post newspaper, and the scene of protest marches

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at being offered a job in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like the old exclamation 'splendid!' and 'post' like a job; they point to the US capital city, home of a famous Post newspaper and of the March on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The American seat of government is a capital city, with a daily paper called the Post.

clue.text: Outcome of Ulster's. disturbances.

definitions.text: Outcome

indicators.note: the Ulster disturbances sound like riots, but here they shake up the letters of the place-name

explanation.surface: Asking what came of the troubles in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbances' shuffles ULSTERS (the apostrophe dropped) into the answer. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequences are what a process ends with, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Abstracts

definitions.text: Abstracts

parts.note: read as a noun, short summaries of longer writings

explanation.walkthrough: The one word could be a verb (takes away) or an adjective; it is the plural noun, summaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed summaries of papers are both called by either word.

clue.text: His heart attacks don't prove fatal

definitions.text: His heart attacks don't prove fatal

parts.words: His heart attacks don't prove fatal
parts.note: heart attacks read as a medical event, but this figure attacks hearts with arrows of love

explanation.surface: A reassuring medical note about a patient's coronaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart attacks' is read medically; the archer of Roman myth attacks hearts, making people fall in love rather than die.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love shoots arrows into hearts, wounding without killing.

clue.text: One might just pop out for a drink

definitions.text: One might just pop out for a drink

parts.words: One might just pop out for a drink
parts.note: popping out for a drink sounds like a trip to the pub, but here a bottle stopper pops out so the drink can be poured

explanation.surface: Someone nipping out briefly to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop out for a drink' is a quick visit to the bar; the thing that pops is the stopper from a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle stopper made of bark is pulled with a pop before the wine is served.

clue.text: This is downright lying

definitions.text: This is downright lying

parts.note: downright lying reads as outright dishonesty, but means lying face down

explanation.surface: An accusation of blatant dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downright' looks like 'utter', and 'lying' like telling lies; together they mean lying with the face downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat with the front of the body downwards is the posture described.

clue.text: Proper respect for the sappers in resisting attacks

definitions.text: Proper respect

indicators.note: the engineers are placed in the middle of the word for resisting attacks

parts.note: defence is the resisting of attack
RE, the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: Due honour to military engineers who held out under assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sappers' is a nickname for the British Army's Royal Engineers, a convention worth knowing; 'resisting attacks' looks like a description of the soldiers, but it is the container word.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous submission to another's wishes or status is a form of respectful regard.

clue.text: Such bad habits can get a hold on one

definitions.text: Such bad habits
can get a hold on one

explanation.surface: Warning that bad habits can take hold of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad habits like smoking are vices, and a vice is also a bench tool whose jaws grip a workpiece, so either kind can get a hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral failings share the name of the clamping tools on a workbench that grip things tight.

clue.text: Not a piece of sweetbread

definitions.text: Not a piece of sweetbread

parts.note: sweetbread is offal, but read as sweet bread it points to a whole sugary loaf, not a slice

explanation.surface: Turning down a serving of offal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetbread is the culinary name for an animal's thymus or pancreas; split as sweet bread it gives a loaf of sugar, the old cone-shaped block sugar was sold in, and a whole one is not a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined sugar was once sold moulded into a tall cone, a whole block of sweet stuff.

clue.text: One fully acquainted with the onions in one particular field

definitions.text: One fully acquainted with the onions in one particular field

parts.words: One fully acquainted with the onions in one particular field
parts.note: 'to know one's onions' is a British idiom for being expert, and the field is a narrow area of knowledge, not a vegetable plot

explanation.surface: A farmer who knows every onion growing in one field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing your onions' is a British idiom for real expertise; 'field' is a subject area, not farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert concentrates on a narrow branch of study and knows it thoroughly.

clue.text: Just the river to cause erosion?

definitions.text: the river
to cause erosion

explanation.surface: Asking whether a river alone could account for the wearing of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham; to wear something is to erode it gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a river of County Durham and the verb for gradual abrasion by use or friction.

clue.text: But he was a big help to the Sherwood Foresters

definitions.text: But he was a big help to the Sherwood Foresters

parts.words: But he was a big help to the Sherwood Foresters
parts.note: the Sherwood Foresters were a British regiment, but here they are Robin Hood's outlaws, and the big helper was the giant ironically nicknamed small

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who assisted a British infantry regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sherwood Foresters were a real regiment; read literally they are Robin Hood's band in Sherwood Forest. 'But' points to the irony of a huge man with a name meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's giant lieutenant was ironically named for smallness despite his great size.

clue.text: Plans that send G.I.s crazy

definitions.text: Plans

indicators.note: soldiers driven crazy suggests their letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers, written without the stops

explanation.surface: Schemes that drive American soldiers mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges SEND and GIS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blueprints or schemes laid out for the future are intended arrangements.

clue.text: Orator with the heart of a giant

definitions.text: Orator with the heart of a giant

parts.words: Orator with the heart of a giant
parts.note: a giant heart sounds like great courage, but the middle letters of this rabble-rouser spell Magog, one of the legendary giants Gog and Magog

explanation.surface: A brave public speaker with great courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of a giant' looks like praise for bravery; the word's own centre holds MAGOG, a giant of British legend paired with Gog.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rousing speaker sways crowds with emotional appeals, an orator of the worst kind.

clue.text: The town's in disorder in Lancashire

definitions.text: in Lancashire

indicators.note: a town in disorder suggests unrest, here it scrambles the letters before it

parts.note: the word read as TOWNS, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A report of rioting in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' shuffles TOWNS and IN into a town of the county named. Lancashire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The place named is a town near Manchester, historically part of that county.

clue.text: For the horse that has 'been docked ?

definitions.text: For the horse that has 'been docked

parts.words: For the horse that has 'been docked
parts.note: a docked horse has had its tail cut short, so what it might want is a piece of tail

explanation.surface: Something provided for a horse whose tail has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Docking a horse cuts its tail short; the answer, an ornament at the end of a book chapter, splits as tail + piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative design at a chapter's close is an end ornament, literally a piece of tail.

clue.text: Aids to hindsight

definitions.text: Aids to hindsight

parts.note: hindsight usually means wisdom after the event, but here it is literally seeing behind you

explanation.surface: Tools for being wise after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hindsight' is read as wisdom after the event; literally it is seeing what is behind, as a driver does with reflecting glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflecting glasses let a driver see what lies behind, literally rear vision.

clue.text: Members of the firing' squad ?

definitions.text: Members of the firing' squad

parts.note: a firing squad usually shoots, but these firing men feed the fires of a steam engine or ship's furnace

explanation.surface: Asking who makes up an execution squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' suggests shooting; it means stoking fires, the job of men who shovel coal into a furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who tend a boiler's fire keep the furnace burning, a crew that fires.

clue.text: Thus ono might come up to scratch

definitions.text: Thus ono might come up to scratch

parts.words: Thus ono might come up to scratch
parts.note: coming up to scratch means meeting the standard, but here one approaches ready to scratch like a cat

explanation.surface: Advice on how to reach an acceptable standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come up to scratch' means reach the required level; read literally, someone approaching with claws out behaves in a feline way.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline behaviour includes scratching with claws, so the adjective describes acting that way.

clue.text: Soldier who starts with a stop

definitions.text: Soldier who starts with a stop

parts.words: Soldier who starts with a stop
parts.note: starting with a stop sounds like a halting march, but the officer's rank begins with the punctuation mark called a colon

explanation.surface: An army man whose career begins with a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: A stop is a punctuation mark; this officer's title starts with the colon (and is said 'kernel').
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army officer ranks above major and below brigadier.

clue.text: It may describe one variety of orgy

definitions.text: It may describe one variety of orgy

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the debauched party take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A word that might sum up a particularly bloody kind of debauch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges ORGY; the whole clue also says the result can describe a bloodthirsty orgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodstained and violent is the sense, fitting a savage revel.

clue.text: They give Pierre that revolutionary look

definitions.text: They give Pierre that revolutionary look

parts.words: They give Pierre that revolutionary look
parts.note: placed before the name Pierre, the garments make ..., leader of the French Revolution's Terror

explanation.surface: Clothes that make a Frenchman look like a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer before PIERRE and you get Robespierre, the French revolutionary leader; the 'look' is a pun on dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Long flowing gowns are garments, and they combine with the French name to give the revolutionary.

clue.text: His efficiency is judged by net results

definitions.text: His efficiency is judged by net results

parts.words: His efficiency is judged by net results
parts.note: net results sounds like final profit, but here it means what ends up in the net of a goal

explanation.surface: A businessman assessed on profit after costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net results' looks like accounting; it is what ends up in the goal net, which a football keeper is judged on.
explanation.definitionFit: The player guarding the goal is assessed by how few shots get into the net.

clue.text: Herrick explained the origin of red ones

definitions.text: Herrick explained the origin of red ones

parts.words: Herrick explained the origin of red ones
parts.note: the poet Robert Herrick wrote a poem titled How ... Came Red

explanation.surface: A writer accounting for where the reds came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red ones' could be anything red, even communists; Robert Herrick, the 17th-century English poet, wrote 'How Roses Came Red'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowers of Herrick's poem are thorny garden blooms, some of them red.

clue.text: Don't go and carry out this order

definitions.text: Don't go and carry out this order

parts.words: Don't go and carry out this order
parts.note: the plea not to leave is also a one-word command which, when obeyed, keeps you put

explanation.surface: A muddled instruction to both leave and remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't go' looks like part of the order; it is the meaning of the one-word command itself, obeyed by remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining where one is answers a request not to leave.

clue.text: One whose answer to " How are you ?"" might be "Middling "?

definitions.text: One whose answer to " How are you ?"" might be "Middling

parts.words: One whose answer to " How are you ?"" might be "Middling
parts.note: 'how are you going?' answered 'between' or 'middling' describes an intermediary, someone who goes in the middle

explanation.surface: Someone who answers a greeting with a lukewarm 'so-so'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middling' reads as 'so-so'; it is literally 'going in the middle', what an intermediary does between two parties.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary carries messages between two parties, standing in the middle.

clue.text: Their occupants get browned off

definitions.text: Their occupants get browned off

parts.note: browned off is slang for fed up, but the roasting joints inside literally turn brown

explanation.surface: People stuck somewhere until they are fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browned off' is British slang for bored or fed up; literally it is what food does when roasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen appliances for baking and roasting turn food brown.

clue.text: Try the third and fourth letters

definitions.text: Try
the third and fourth letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to attempt a pair of letters in a word.
explanation.walkthrough: To essay is to try. The word's third and fourth letters are S and A, and its spelling is those letters' names, ESS and AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempting something is making an essay of it; ESS and AY name the letters S and A.

clue.text: Not the sort of gags to get encores

definitions.text: Not the sort of gags to get encores

parts.words: Not the sort of gags to get encores
parts.note: gags read as jokes, but here they are devices that muffle sound, so no applause is heard

explanation.surface: A comic's jokes that fail to win calls for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gags' looks like jokes; it means things that stop noise, like the mufflers fitted to guns or engines.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that muffle a gun or exhaust stop the noise, a mechanical gag.
